compatNote: COMPATIBILITY FLOOR the base states and every addition inherits (v5 version spine, V5-PLAN 2.2). Floors plus a single proven point, never a support matrix: rolling latest-only means the gate proves exactly one (dw, apps, swift tag) triple per run, and what it proved is recorded upward in layers/INDEX.json gateProven - written by the Foundry, never by hand. `dw.min` is the platform floor, `dw.tfm` the single target framework the host must build against, `swift.tag` the dynamicweb/Swift release tag (the 3-digit `swiftVersion` above is the same release without the tag form). `apps[].required: false` is an optional companion app: absent is fine, present below `min` is not. An addition MAY restate `compat` in its own layer.json to raise a floor; it may never lower one.
minSerializerVersionDeprecated: DEPRECATED ALIAS, not a second floor. The one serializer floor is compat.apps[id=Truvio.Commerce.Serializer].min: the Foundry compat leg (Test-CompatFloors) and the dw-demo-base install step read that key and nothing else. This field repeats the same value for prose readers that still name it (dynamicweb/skills dw-users-permissions page-gating.md); tools/ci/Validate-Distribution.ps1 fails when it disagrees with compat.apps, so it can never state a different number. Raise compat.apps and this field together; remove this field once no reader names it.
serializerTaughtSurfaceNote: WHY THE FLOOR IS 1.0.2-beta (base 3.4.2). Layers now ship serialized SqlTable rows: truvio-demo 1.8.0 ships its commerce dataset as merge-mode SqlTable YAML with a per-document ownership header (Foundry #1215), and sample-data 3.0.0 follows. Three engine facts set the floor. (1) SqlTable NULL round trip: Truvio.Commerce.Serializer 1.0.1-beta and earlier wrote a NULL column as 1900-01-01 / '' / 0 in Merge mode on a row where an empty-string column came before the NULL (Serializer issue #18); 1.0.2-beta is the first release that writes it back as NULL, so an older engine silently corrupts shipped rows. (2) PackageUnzip, the transport an online build uses to move a layer's files, is available from 1.0.1-beta. (3) The ownership header needs 1.0.0-beta or later: a 0.9.x engine fails strict on the unknown ownership column. The engine's taught surface (the skills corpus and the Foundry harness) may run ahead of this floor; the floor rises only when a layer ships something an older engine drops, rejects or corrupts. Raise compat.apps[id=Truvio.Commerce.Serializer].min and minSerializerVersion together, not this note.
description: Machine-readable guarantees the base layer makes to every addition (v3.0 Distribution, base 3.0.0 FRAMEWORK-ONLY). The Swift 2.4 base split moved ALL content (both mode trees) and UrlPath to the surface-swift layer; the base now ships only the framework SQL sets + this contract + SQL-predicate config. Additions (feature/sample-data/surface/theme layers) bind ONLY to this contract - never to each other. Content-scoped contract bits (content areas, langPrefix, navDepth, page anchors, title rules, per-environment Area exclusions, protected Swift item types) moved to layers/surface-swift/surface.contract-notes.json. The gate reads this file for the base-contract collision check.

idRules.nvarcharPkNote: When an addition writes rows into a base-owned table whose PK is nvarchar (most Ecom tables - PriceId, PaymentId, ProductId, etc.), it MUST namespace the PK with a PACK-<NAME>- prefix (uppercase layer name). Keeps additions disjoint from the base and from each other.
idRules.intIdentityNote: When an addition writes SqlTable rows keyed by an int-identity PK, it MUST reserve an id at or above the 100000 floor. The floor does not reach _content item-instance ids (ItemType_<systemName> rows written through a page or paragraph): ItemType_* Id is a non-identity nvarchar the platform allocates on insert, and the Serializer content provider re-creates item rows by page/paragraph uniqueId, so the target assigns its own id and a YAML fields.Id never lands as the stored id. fields.Id in _content is informational only; no validator checks an item-id floor on _content. The floor applies to the int ids a layer MINTS. The AccessUser ids this contract names in guaranteedRows are explicit exceptions: the permission groups 1325 / 1270 / 1292 (base-owned) and the sample-data personas 1326 / 1328 sit below the floor by contract, and a layer MAY ship exactly those ids as SqlTable rows (the base ships the groups; sample-data ships the personas and their memberships). Any other id below 100000 is out of contract. No validator checks the int-identity floor; it is an authoring rule.
idRules.baseCatalogNote: The base ships ZERO catalog (scaffolding-only, swift/2.3.2): EcomGroups, EcomProducts, EcomGroupProductRelation, EcomVariantGroups, EcomVariantsOptions, EcomVariantOptionsProductRelation, EcomDiscount, EcomDiscountTranslation, EcomPrices carry no base rows. The collision surface for these tables is addition-vs-sample-data-vs-addition, arbitrated statically by the gate.
idRules.reservedFixtureNote: The sample-data layer's demo catalog (merge/_sql/catalog.sql) reserves these key prefixes. Additions must not use them.
idRules.noPerItemTypeNumericTableNote: The contract is prefix-based, not per-itemType-numeric. There is deliberately NO per-itemType numeric range table - do not invent one.

guaranteedRows.permissionGroupsNote: DW 10.26.9 has no AccessUserGroup table - groups ARE AccessUser rows of type 2.
guaranteedRows.usersNote: users and memberships are NOT base rows. They ship in the sample-data layer (merge/_sql/identities.sql, sample-data layer.json sql[0]) and every entry carries presentOnlyWhen: sampleData - they exist only when an edition activates sampleData: true. An edition with sampleData: false has no AccessUser 1328 / 1326 and no memberships, so a sign-in, persona or customer-number binding against them finds no row. A layer probe that needs them names the fixture in its requiresFixtures. Only permissionGroups are base-owned (baseOwnedTables.replaceFiltered FILTER-01).

referenceCategory.note: Hidden template category (CategoryType 2) required by DemoVerifier Check 2. Seeded pre-host-start (DW caches at startup).

contractPrice.note: Ships in the sample-data layer's catalog.sql, next to the product it scopes to; present only when an edition activates sampleData: true.

anchors.note: The buyer and CSR anchors name the sample-data rows in guaranteedRows.users: present only when an edition activates sampleData: true. Content anchors (area 3, langPrefix /swift-2) moved to surface-swift (base 3.0.0 ships zero content areas).

repositories.name: ProductsFrontend
repositories.note: ProductsFrontend is the storefront search repository the Swift design package ships (Files/System/Repositories/ProductsFrontend/ at the Swift 2.4.0 tag, alongside ProductsBackend). No layer in this Distribution ships it: it arrives with the host's Swift Files overlay, which is why provisionedByGate is false. Every eCom_ProductCatalog surface this Distribution ships binds it by path - surface-swift Shop PLP (IndexQuery + FacetGroups), surface-swift desktop header search, surface-swift Express Buy, surface-dap-portal Product Assets and Search results, feature-bom-configurator Kit Configurator. A storefront PLP that cannot list products answers HTTP 200 in both of its failure shapes, never a 500. (1) Repository present over an index of zero documents: the page carries an in-page dw-error block with the Lucene 'numHits must be > 0' ArgumentException. (2) Repository absent: the catalog app renders an EMPTY swift-v2_app div with no product list, no facet rail and no error text of any kind, so the page passes a status scan AND an error-text scan while showing nothing. Gate the PLP on a positive subject (at least one product-card element) plus dw-error == 0, never on HTTP status or on the absence of error text alone.

currencyRates.note: EcomCurrencies.CurrencyRate is hundredths against the default currency. The default (EUR, CurrencyIsDefault true on every EUR$$<lang> row) carries 100. A non-default currency at rate 1 renders every price in it a hundred times over, with correct symbol and culture formatting, no error and no log entry (measured on DW 10.28.10: a stored 45.00 served as $4,500.00 at USD rate 1). USD, the currency the Swift storefront serves, ships at 100: one-to-one parity with the default, a deliberate demo value and not an exchange rate. No shipped row carries a rate at or below 1. The other non-default rows carry the values of the source solution and are not maintained exchange rates; a solution that needs real conversion sets real rates, keeping the default at 100 and every other rate relative to it.

replaceFiltered.note: FILTER-01: only the three permission groups are base-owned on AccessUser; user rows (1328/1326) are seeded, not serialized into the base.

baseOwnedTables.note: Additions touching a base-owned table follow idRules (prefix / floor) and must pass the static intersection checks below. Base ships zero catalog (see idRules.baseCatalog) and zero content areas (base split 3.0.0). UrlPath is surface-swift-owned (its single row is a friendly-URL redirect bound to area 3 + a Swift page id - no route targets exist in a framework-only base).

collisionChecks.rule: Intersect an addition's _sql/<Table>/*.yml filenames (= row keys; composite keys join with $$) with the base's filenames for the same table. Non-empty = FAIL.
WR-10: the same table+filename shipped by >1 active addition = FAIL. A single layer shipping the same key in its own replace+merge is NOT a collision.

07-01: an addition's fragment-shipped _content relative paths must be disjoint from base _content paths (union of both mode trees); cross-layer parity; shipped-files-only (referenced base anchors excluded); declared-footprint parity (every Content entry matches a declared fragmentContent {areaId, path}).

WR-04: (itemType, fields.Id) pairs land as PK rows in shared ItemType_<systemName> tables. The same pair by >1 owner = FAIL. Reusing an id NUMBER across DIFFERENT itemType tables is fine (PK surface is per-table).

registrationAsymmetry.rule: Every csLedger entry with registration 'addin-attribute-config-row' MUST have >=1 matching configRows entry.
registrationAsymmetry.note: Cross-field rule enforced at activation (not JSON-Schema-expressible); locked by tests.

movedToSurfaceSwift.note: Moved by the base split (Swift 2.4 roll-forward): perEnvironmentAreaExclusions, protectedItemTypes, content anchors (areas/langPrefix), navDepth obligation, title-integrity rules. See layers/surface-swift/surface.contract-notes.json.
